What does explain the spread is local structure preservation of the code space. In DPLM-2 a one-bit codeword error costs 0.019 TM where a random codeword costs 0.347, and the trained model's own errors are correspondingly local, at 0.51 of the random Hamming expectation; FoldToken4 fails both tests at the same codebook size and is 0.13 TM less writable. Three controls discipline how such a benchmark may be read. A same-recipe rerun puts the noise floor at $σ=0.0067$ TM, which collapses an apparent six-way ranking into four tiers. A reference-free geometry panel turns out to be nearly orthogonal to TM (Pearson $-0.58$), with the worst arm by TM producing the most physically valid backbones. And two pre-registered interventions are null for a reason the mechanism measurements reveal: the quantity they target saturates at 1.5B tokens while TM is still rising. All 131 evaluation cells, including raw generated token streams, are released.
items.title_ko: 언어 모델의 생성 목표로서 단백질 구조 토크나이저 벤치마킹
items.summary_ko: 단백질 3D 구조를 언어 모델에 전달하는 표준 방식인 이산 구조 토크나이저(discrete structure tokenizers)의 평가 기준이 재구성 충실도(reconstruction fidelity)에만 초점을 맞추는 문제를 지적합니다. 이 연구는 모델이 토크나이저를 얼마나 잘 '작성(write)'할 수 있는지 직접 측정하는 '작성 가능성(writability)' 지표를 도입하고 9B 모델을 벤치마킹합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 기반 단백질 설계에서 언어 모델의 구조 생성 능력을 더욱 정확하게 평가하고 개선할 수 있는 새로운 방법론을 제시합니다. 바이오인포매틱스 및 AI 신약 개발 분야 개발자에게 중요한 평가 도구를 제공합니다.

items.title: RightDiff: Learning Generative Reward Models to Judge by the Right Differences
items.body: Generative reward models typically rely on generic query-level rubrics or unconstrained rationales, overlooking the fact that pairwise preference is driven by response-specific differences. Moreover, optimizing solely for outcome correctness encourages models to exploit superficial shortcuts such as verbosity and formatting, triggering rationale drift. To address this, we propose RightDiff, which structures pairwise evaluation into an evidence-grounded evaluation trajectory executed in a single autoregressive generation. RightDiff explicitly discovers contrastive differences between candidates, categorizes them into material or immaterial factors, and induces pair-specific rubrics before final adjudication. To train this process without post-hoc rationalization, we synthesize demonstration data via response-isolated prompts and optimize the reward model with a difference-alignment reward regularized by budget-constrained one-to-one matching and multiplicative gating. RightDiff achieves state-of-the-art preference modeling performance on RewardBench and RM-Bench, surpassing all open-source reward models and leading proprietary LLM judges. Downstream, it provides reliable supervision for direct preference optimization on Arena-Hard and AlpacaEval while effectively resisting length shortcuts.

items.title: Making Evaluation Explicit Is Not Enough: Supervising the Evaluation Process in Generative Reward Models
items.body: Generative reward models (GRMs) make language-model evaluation more explicit by generating critiques, rubrics, or intermediate analyses before predicting a final preference. However, explicit evaluation does not necessarily imply a reliable evaluation process: under outcome-only supervision, a model may reach the correct final preference while producing weak or unsupported intermediate judgments, turning the evaluation into a post-hoc rationalization. We introduce STEP-GRM, a framework that directly supervises the intermediate evaluation process of rubric-based GRMs. In addition to conventional preference supervision, STEP-GRM provides structural guidance for rubric construction and local supervision for criterion-level judgments, encouraging the model to learn not only the correct final preference but also a more reliable process for reaching it. Extensive experiments show that STEP-GRM achieves strong performance on standard reward-modeling benchmarks while improving the consistency and correctness of intermediate evaluations. Moreover, reward signals produced by STEP-GRM lead to better downstream policy optimization, demonstrating that more reliable evaluation processes can translate into practical gains beyond reward-model accuracy.
items.title_ko: 평가 명시화만으로는 부족: 생성형 보상 모델의 평가 프로세스 감독
items.summary_ko: 생성형 보상 모델(GRM)이 명시적인 평가(critiques, rubrics)를 생성하더라도, 결과 중심의 감독만으로는 신뢰할 수 없는 평가 프로세스를 가질 수 있음을 지적합니다. STEP-GRM 프레임워크는 평가 프로세스 자체를 직접 감독합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 평가 모델의 투명성과 신뢰성을 높이는 데 필수적인 연구입니다. 모델이 올바른 최종 결론에 도달하는 동시에 약하거나 근거 없는 중간 판단을 내리는 '합리화(rationalization)' 문제를 해결하려는 개발자에게 중요합니다.

items.title: Breaking the Binary-Lifting Barrier for DNA Minimizer Density: Exact Optimization of a Native 4-ary Order at (w, k) = (12, 5)
items.body: Minimizer schemes sample at least one $k$-mer from every window of $w$ consecutive $k$-mers via a total order $π$ on $Σ^k$. For DNA ($σ= 4$), state-of-the-art lookup schemes such as GreedyMini and OptMini optimize a binary order ($2^k$ ranks) and lift it to $Σ^k$ by ranking one bit-plane primarily and breaking $2^k$-way ties lexicographically on the other bit-plane. At $(w, k) = (12, 5)$, this projection locks sets of $32$ DNA $5$-mers into contiguous blocks and restricts the active universal hitting set (UHS) prefix to $448$ of $1024$ $5$-mers, giving exact expected DNA density $2246214544 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1307468945$ for OptMini (k5-w12-13.txt) and $2248978620 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1309077849$ for GreedyMini (w12_k5.gm). We bypass binary lifting and optimize directly over native $4$-ary permutations ($|Σ^k| = 1024$) from scratch via: (i) an exact de Bruijn endpoint transfer-matrix dynamic program over $B(4, 4)$ ($256$ states), (ii) a weighted set-cover ratio initializer (SetCover4) producing a compact $U = 314$ UHS prefix, (iii) bitmask-sparse simulated annealing preserving the zero-cost $w$-walk-free tail invariant, and (iv) two-pass $O(N)$ exact best-insertion sweeps with large-neighborhood ruin-and-recreate search. The resulting explicit $4$-ary order achieves exact expected DNA density $2234289615 / 2^{34} \approx 0.130052772292$ (density factor $1.690686$), cutting charged windows by $11924929$ contexts ($-0.530890\%$ relative) below OrensteinLab/Minimizers and $14689005$ ($-0.653141\%$) below w12_k5.gm at $8200$-byte lookup storage ($1280$ bytes bit-packed). Warm-start relaxation stalls at $U = 379$ ($0.1301728789$), whereas native $4$-ary initialization breaks $32/32$ high-bit blocks across all $2+2$ nucleotide partitions.
items.title_ko: DNA 미니마이저 밀도의 이진 리프팅 장벽 돌파: 네이티브 4진법 순서의 정확한 최적화
items.summary_ko: DNA 시퀀싱에서 사용되는 미니마이저(minimizer) 방식의 효율성을 향상시키기 위해, 기존의 이진 순서(binary order) 기반 접근 방식의 한계를 지적하고, (w, k) = (12, 5) 조건에서 네이티브 4진법 순서를 정확히 최적화하는 방법을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: 생물 정보학 분야에서 대규모 DNA/RNA 시퀀스 데이터 처리 효율성을 높이는 핵심 기술입니다. 유전체 분석 및 관련 AI 모델 개발자에게 더욱 최적화된 자료 구조 및 알고리즘 설계를 위한 기반 지식을 제공합니다.

items.title: RetraQ: Manifold-Constrained Critic Guidance for Flow Policies in RL
items.body: A learned critic can improve a pretrained flow-matching policy by steering sampled actions toward higher predicted value. However, even a critic that fits the behavior data well can provide misleading action gradients. Gradient components pointing away from the data-supported region are weakly constrained by behavior data and can lead guidance to exploit critic extrapolation errors. We introduce RetraQ (Retraction-based Q-guidance), which uses geometry encoded by the pretrained flow to constrain both the direction and the destination of critic guidance. A single velocity evaluation of the frozen flow defines a denoising map. RetraQ filters the critic gradient with the map's Jacobian and applies the map itself to correct the updated action. Our analysis characterizes when these operations approximate tangent filtering and retraction onto the behavior manifold. The same update guides actions at test time and provides targets for policy distillation and online reinforcement learning. In controlled studies, RetraQ improves true return while keeping refined actions close to the data-supported region, and its distillation targets remain more stable than those of raw critic ascent. In offline-to-online training on LIBERO and OGBench, RetraQ achieves higher mean final success than the evaluated critic-guidance baselines. On a real-world plug-insertion task, test-time RetraQ improves the success rate of a behavior-cloned $π_{0.5}$ policy from 55.0% to 76.7%. Online training further increases success to 98.3% in only 30 minutes and 100% within one hour. Project page: https://2027ICLR.github.io/retraq/
items.title_ko: RetraQ: RL의 흐름 정책을 위한 매니폴드 제약 비평가 안내
items.summary_ko: 학습된 비평가(critic)가 사전 학습된 흐름 매칭 정책(flow-matching policy)의 성능을 향상시킬 수 있지만, 데이터 지원 영역 밖으로 벗어나는 행동 기울기(action gradients)는 비평가의 외삽 오류(extrapolation errors)를 악용할 수 있습니다. RetraQ는 사전 학습된 흐름으로 인코딩된 기하학을 사용하여 행동을 제약합니다.
items.why_ko: 강화 학습(RL) 에이전트의 안정성과 효율성을 향상시키는 데 기여하며, 특히 행동 공간이 복잡한 로봇 제어와 같은 분야에서 모델이 신뢰할 수 없는 예측을 악용하는 것을 방지하는 데 중요한 기술입니다.

items.title: ARS-VLM: Visually Aligned Augmented Random Search for Vision-Language Models
items.body: First-order reinforcement learning, such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), is widely used to post-train Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for multimodal reasoning. However, it incurs heavy memory and system overhead from backpropagation, optimizer states, and a reference model. Forward-only zeroth-order (ZO) methods, such as Evolution Strategies (ES) and its top-k variant Augmented Random Search (ARS), avoid these overheads via reward-guided weight perturbations, yet remain unexplored for VLM reasoning. We find that directly applying standard ES or vanilla ARS to VLMs suffers from two fundamental failure modes: (i) patch-grid overfitting, fitting fragile grid-specific visual token artifacts while ignoring spatial invariants, and (ii) catastrophic forgetting, degrading general perception and out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks due to unbounded high-rank parameter and policy drift. We propose ARS-VLM, a visually aligned Augmented Random Search framework for forward-only VLM post-training. First, ARS-VLM extracts a contrastive visual basis from bilinearly paired cross-grid views, concentrating perturbations on shared visual signals while suppressing patch-shift artifacts. Second, ARS-VLM anchors shallow visual-fusion layers with a soft subspace prior while freeing deep reasoning layers, restraining policy drift without a reference model. Third, ARS-VLM scores perturbations on paired views to discard view-fragile directions during top-k selection. We evaluate ARS-VLM on Qwen3-VL-4B and Qwen3-VL-8B on multimodal reasoning tasks. On 8B, ARS-VLM reaches 61.0% validation accuracy in 20 steps versus 150 for GRPO (7.5x fewer optimization steps) and avoids the late OOD collapse of vanilla ARS and ES. Moreover, ARS-VLM achieves 75.41% single-view micro accuracy across seven OOD vision reasoning benchmarks, compared with 75.31% for full-parameter GRPO, using forward-only post-training.
items.title_ko: ARS-VLM: 시각적으로 정렬된 증강 무작위 탐색을 통한 Vision-Language 모델 후처리
items.summary_ko: 그룹 상대 정책 최적화(GRPO)와 같은 1차 강화 학습 방법이 VLM(Vision-Language Models)의 멀티모달 추론 후처리 학습에 사용되지만, 메모리 및 시스템 오버헤드가 크다는 한계가 있습니다. ARS-VLM은 순방향 전용 0차 방법인 증강 무작위 탐색(ARS)을 시각적으로 정렬하여 이러한 오버헤드를 피합니다.
items.why_ko: VLM의 학습 효율성을 높이고, 특히 리소스 제약이 있는 환경에서 멀티모달 추론 모델을 효과적으로 미세 조정하는 방법을 제시합니다.

items.title: Calibrated Reading of Latent Reasoning and Communication
items.body: Latent reasoning and key-value communication store intermediate information in continuous representations, limiting direct inspection of model behavior. Existing activation readers trade the low cost of task-specific probes against the flexibility of language-model decoders. We propose the Calibrated Latent Reader, CLR, a compact transformer that predicts reasoning outcomes and message content through task-conditioned interactions between states and candidate answers. Source adapters support transfer across models, while conformal calibration provides coverage and false-alarm guarantees under exchangeability. On two CODI models, CLR improves accuracy over MLP and attention probes by 4-18 percentage points for final-answer prediction and reference-value membership. On CODI-GPT-2, it achieves accuracy comparable to a 1.7B LatentQA-based verbalizer using 437-648 times fewer inference FLOPs. On synthetic Qwen3-4B communications, comparing decoded facts with public commitments detects 93.1% of message substitutions at a nominal 5% false-positive rate.
items.title_ko: 잠재 추론 및 통신의 보정된 읽기
items.summary_ko: 잠재 추론(latent reasoning) 및 키-값 통신(key-value communication)이 중간 정보를 연속적 표현으로 저장하여 모델 동작을 직접 검사하기 어렵게 만드는 문제를 다룹니다. 이 연구는 태스크 조건부 상호작용을 통해 추론 결과와 메시지 내용을 예측하는 컴팩트한 트랜스포머인 CLR(Calibrated Latent Reader)을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델의 '블랙박스' 내부 작동을 이해하고 해석하는 데 중요한 도구를 제공하며, 모델의 의사결정 과정을 시각화하고 디버깅하는 데 도움을 줍니다.

items.title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation
items.body: In embedding-based video anomaly detection (VAD), normal clips can have high similarity to anomalous descriptions, an anomaly bias that leads to false positives. Methods such as PRISM mitigate this bias by measuring deviations from a normality reference along anomaly directions. Both the normality reference and the anomaly directions are derived from text and shared across videos, although normal activity and the appearance of anomalies vary across scenes. The resulting scores are also sensitive to prompt selection. To address these limitations, we propose Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation (VIDE), a training-free framework that adapts text-derived scoring to each test video using frozen clip embeddings. VIDE estimates normal scene content from clips with low initial anomaly scores and uses this estimate to partially correct the textual reference. It then rescales category responses, penalizes clips with strong responses across categories, and refines the anomaly directions using high-scoring clips. VIDE averages scores across prompt views to reduce sensitivity to prompt selection and fuses scores from two frozen encoders. With both encoders, VIDE improves AUC over the best PRISM result by $1.5$, $1.9$, and $3.5$ points on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD, respectively, and AP by $6.5$ points on XD-Violence and $9.3$ points on MSAD. VIDE yields the highest AUC among the compared training-free methods on all three benchmarks and the highest reported AUC among all compared methods on XD-Violence and MSAD. Our code is included in the supplementary material and will be made publicly available.
items.title_ko: VIDE: 시각적 내재 분포 추정을 통한 훈련 없는 비디오 이상 감지
items.summary_ko: 임베딩 기반 비디오 이상 감지(VAD)에서 정상 클립이 이상 설명과 높은 유사성을 보여 오탐(false positives)을 유발하는 문제를 해결하기 위해, 장면별로 정규성 기준과 이상 방향을 학습하는 훈련 없는(training-free) 방법인 VIDE(Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation)를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 감시, 보안, 제조 등 다양한 분야에서 실시간 비디오 이상 감지 시스템의 정확성과 효율성을 높이는 데 기여합니다. 특히 레이블링된 이상 데이터가 부족한 경우에도 적용 가능한 실용적인 접근법입니다.

items.title: Interpretable Orthogonal Latent Diffusion with Scale-Selective Uncertainty for Medical Image Super-Resolution
items.body: Diffusion models are increasingly used for medical image reconstruction and super-resolution, but their samples may contain plausible fine-scale hallucinations that are difficult to identify from the reconstructed image alone. We propose Med-PODiff, a patch-wise proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) diffusion framework for brain MRI super-resolution that performs generative reconstruction in compact and interpretable local coefficient spaces. Unlike pixel-space or learned-latent diffusion models, Med-PODiff uses the POD structure to separate low-rank anatomical variation from fine-detail residual variation, enabling predictive uncertainty to be decomposed into total, coarse, and fine components. Building on this decomposition, we define a pixel-wise hallucination-risk score, $H_p$, that emphasizes regions where fine-detail uncertainty dominates coarse structural uncertainty. On brain MRI, Med-PODiff outperforms representative diffusion baselines in reconstruction quality while producing well-calibrated predictive intervals, with total uncertainty detecting high-error regions at AUROC 0.954. More importantly, the decomposed uncertainty is scale-selective: coarse and fine uncertainty preferentially predict errors at the corresponding scales, with $H_p$ localizing fine error at AUROC $0.906$. Controlled injections and retrospective Cartesian $k$-space undersampling further support fine-detail localization and degradation robustness. The discarded POD tail is only $3.8\%$ of the retained fine-error magnitude, and Med-PODiff improves downstream segmentation consistency while requiring substantially less inference time than pixel-space diffusion.
items.title_ko: 의료 영상 초해상도를 위한 스케일 선택적 불확실성을 갖춘 해석 가능한 직교 잠재 확산
items.summary_ko: 의료 영상 재구성 및 초해상도(super-resolution)에 확산 모델을 사용할 때 발생하는 '그럴듯한 환각(plausible hallucinations)' 문제를 해결하기 위해, 패치 단위 POD(Proper Orthogonal Decomposition) 확산 프레임워크인 Med-PODiff를 제안합니다. 이는 생성적 재구성을 컴팩트하고 해석 가능한 지역 계수 공간에서 수행합니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 영상 진단 AI의 신뢰성과 안전성을 향상시키는 데 기여합니다. 특히 의료 분야에서는 '환각'이 오진으로 이어질 수 있으므로, 이를 제어하고 해석 가능한 결과를 제공하는 기술은 매우 중요합니다.

items.title: Rethinking Reasoning Effort Training in Large Language Models: On-Policy Distillation or Reinforcement Learning?
items.body: Large language models have shown strong capabilities on complex tasks, yet how to control their reasoning effort remains a significant challenge for practical deployment. This paper provides a systematic investigation of reasoning-effort training, contrasting reinforcement learning (RL) with on-policy distillation (OPD). We find that compressing reasoning and separating effort tiers are governed by different signals. Length-penalized RL reliably compresses a single policy, reducing thinking on AIME25 by 70\% without accuracy loss, but collapses the tiers when they are trained jointly. Multi-teacher OPD separates them: across 33 benchmarks, low and medium use 58\% and 43\% fewer thinking tokens than high, while high improves on the reference policy by 3.1 points. We trace this difference to the training signal. A sequence-level reward cannot tell tier-specific behavior from shared behavior, whereas OPD supplies a tier-specific target at every visited state, including the decision to stop. Building on this analysis, we show that a single token-level KL anchor on the high tier is sufficient to learn separated tiers within one RL stage, and that natural-language effort instructions make this separation emerge from the start of training, yielding a policy competitive with multi-teacher OPD at matched thinking length. Finally, the separation built by dense targets holds only on the states seen in training: it does not carry over to unseen agentic tasks, where effort acts mainly through the number of interaction turns, whereas the compression induced by sequence-level rewards does.
items.title_ko: LLM 추론 노력 훈련 재고: 온-정책 증류인가 강화 학습인가?
items.summary_ko: LLM의 '추론 노력(reasoning effort)'을 제어하는 방법에 대한 체계적인 연구로, 강화 학습(RL)과 온-정책 증류(OPD)를 비교합니다. 이 연구는 추론 압축과 노력 단계 분리가 서로 다른 신호에 의해 좌우됨을 발견했습니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 복잡한 작업에서 필요한 만큼만 추론하여 응답 속도와 비용 효율성을 최적화하는 데 기여합니다. LLM의 추론 제어 메커니즘을 이해하고 최적화하려는 개발자에게 중요한 실무적 지식을 제공합니다.

items.title: Bit-Flip Attacks on Quantized Neural Networks without Knowledge of Model Parameters
items.body: We show that quantization asymmetry concentrates bit-flip vulnerability in small tensors retained at high precision. CoarseHammer targets these tensors and accepts flips at any bit, without parameter values, gradients, or data. It remains effective under continued fine-tuning. Under ideal placement, CoarseHammer reaches chance accuracy in at least 81.5% of runs on each of ten evaluated models, including four large language models, with median successful runs requiring at most 24 flips. On simulated DRAM with 0.01 flippable bits per million, it outperforms three prior attacks on every evaluated convolutional network, succeeding in up to 83.6% of runs while they never succeed. On a real system, CoarseHammer steers heap-allocated tensors onto vulnerable frames despite address space layout randomization, without accessing the model file. With 16 templated frames, median accuracy reaches chance for all four language models and approximately chance for four convolutional networks.
items.body_ko: 우리는 양자화 비대칭(quantization asymmetry)이 높은 정밀도로 유지되는 작은 텐서에 비트-플립 취약점(bit-flip vulnerability)을 집중시킨다는 것을 보여줍니다. CoarseHammer는 이러한 텐서를 표적으로 삼고, 파라미터 값, 기울기 또는 데이터 없이 어떤 비트에서도 플립을 허용합니다. 이는 지속적인 파인튜닝(fine-tuning) 하에서도 효과적입니다. 이상적인 배치에서, CoarseHammer는 10개의 평가된 모델(4개의 대규모 언어 모델 포함) 각각에서 최소 81.5%의 실행에서 우연 정확도(chance accuracy)에 도달하며, 성공적인 실행의 중간값은 최대 24개의 플립을 필요로 합니다. 100만 비트당 0.01개의 플립 가능한 비트를 가진 시뮬레이션된 DRAM에서, 이는 평가된 모든 컨볼루션 네트워크에서 이전 세 가지 공격을 능가하며, 최대 83.6%의 실행에서 성공하는 반면, 이전 공격들은 전혀 성공하지 못합니다. 실제 시스템에서 CoarseHammer는 주소 공간 레이아웃 무작위화(address space layout randomization)에도 불구하고 모델 파일에 접근하지 않고 힙 할당된 텐서를 취약한 프레임으로 유도합니다. 16개의 템플릿 프레임으로, 모든 4개의 언어 모델에서 중간 정확도가 우연 수준에 도달하고, 4개의 컨볼루션 네트워크에서는 대략 우연 수준에 도달합니다.
items.title_ko: 모델 파라미터 지식 없이 양자화된 신경망에 대한 비트 플립 공격
items.summary_ko: 양자화된 신경망(Quantized Neural Networks)에 대한 새로운 비트 플립 공격(Bit-Flip Attacks)인 CoarseHammer를 소개합니다. 이 공격은 모델 파라미터에 대한 지식 없이, 양자화 비대칭(quantization asymmetry)이 비트 플립 취약점을 고정밀로 유지되는 작은 텐서에 집중시킨다는 점을 악용합니다.
items.why_ko: 양자화된 AI 모델의 보안에 대한 심각한 취약점을 드러냅니다. 엣지 디바이스 등 실제 환경에 배포되는 경량화된 AI 모델의 보안을 강화하고 악의적인 공격으로부터 보호하기 위한 방어 메커니즘 개발의 중요성을 강조합니다.

items.title: EnSurv: Deep Generative Survival Modeling with Application to Kidney Graft Outcomes
items.body: Kidney transplantation is the optimal treatment for life-threatening end-stage renal disease, providing significant survival advantages over dialysis. Given the severe shortage of donor organs, accurately predicting the time to premature graft failure is an essential clinical task for optimizing organ allocation and tailoring individualized immunosuppressive therapies. This study is motivated by a comprehensive United Network of Organ Sharing (UNOS) dataset containing 243,443 kidney transplant records with complex multi-region structures and high right-censoring rates. We propose EnSurv (survival engression), a deep generative survival framework designed to capture complex, non-linear clinical covariate interactions for modeling time to graft failure. Within a pre-additive noise model (pre-ANM) family, EnSurv optimizes an energy score augmented with pooled Kaplan-Meier tail completion to handle right-censoring. We identify the pooled-completion target of the objective, establish consistency for its best approximation within the pre-ANM family, and give conditions and error bounds for its relation to true conditional graft survival. EnSurv also provides global explainability through summaries of fitted feature weights and incorporates domain constraints through established clinical directions using a soft gradient penalty. Extensive simulation experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method in comparison with existing methods. Application to the UNOS cohort demonstrates that EnSurv effectively models individual and region-level effects, consistently outperforming baselines across evaluation metrics encompassing discrimination, calibration, and accuracy.
items.title_ko: EnSurv: 신장 이식 결과 적용을 위한 딥 생성형 생존 모델링
items.summary_ko: 생명을 위협하는 말기 신장 질환의 최적 치료법인 신장 이식에서, 조기 이식 실패 시간을 정확하게 예측하는 임상적 과제를 해결하기 위해 '딥 생성형 생존 모델링(Deep Generative Survival Modeling)' 프레임워크인 EnSurv를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 분야에서 AI 기반 생존 분석 모델의 발전을 보여줍니다. 장기 이식 결과 예측 및 개인화된 치료법 개발에 기여하여 의료 서비스의 질을 향상시킬 수 있습니다.

items.title: CoverMem: Coverage-Constrained Visual Memory for Budgeted Embodied Question Answering
items.body: Episodic-memory embodied question answering enables agents to answer questions based on previously recorded visual observations of the surrounding scenes. However, growing observation histories, varying observation quality across viewpoints, and limited computational resources make it challenging to construct and maintain compact visual memories while retrieving sufficient evidence for question answering. To address these challenges, we introduce CoverMem, which incorporates three key components: (1) a coverage-constrained memory construction method that selects a compact set of informative full frames satisfying object-quality and representative-scene coverage requirements; (2) a coverage-preserving incremental maintenance strategy that locally reselects only the affected frames to satisfy updated coverage requirements as observations arrive; and (3) a budgeted complementary frame selection method that balances question relevance, additional support for question requirements, and redundancy with selected frames within a fixed budget. Experimental results on three benchmarks covering diverse environments and question types demonstrate that CoverMem improves question-answering performance under limited visual budgets.
items.title_ko: CoverMem: 예산 제약 환경의 시각-질의 응답을 위한 커버리지 제약 시각 메모리
items.summary_ko: 에이전트가 이전에 기록된 시각적 관찰을 기반으로 질문에 답변하는 '에피소드 메모리 기반 시각-질의 응답(Episodic-memory embodied question answering)'에서, 증가하는 관찰 이력, 다양한 관찰 품질, 제한된 자원 문제를 해결하기 위한 CoverMem 프레임워크를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 자율 에이전트 및 로봇의 효율적인 시각 메모리 관리 및 정보 검색 능력 향상에 기여합니다. 제한된 컴퓨팅 자원에서 장기적인 시각 정보를 효과적으로 활용해야 하는 개발자에게 중요합니다.

items.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Classifier Chains
items.body: Multi-label classification continues to be relevant to a variety of modern tasks. Among other challenges, modern data sets are increasingly large with respect to the number of labels, and these labels may be noisy or missing in the training sets. Label-wise scores and ranking-based metrics have been popular, but optimising exact multi-label evaluation (where a predicted set of labels should match the true set exactly) is particularly relevant for many domains, e.g., in medicine; alongside some measure of confidence. This requires an estimation of joint probability across labels (a model of label dependence; conditioned on each input instance). A family of methods known as probabilistic classifier chains provides such inference. However, these existing varieties either do not scale to a large number of labels or do so by approximating joint via marginal distributions in a way that compromises the estimation of uncertainty for exact match accuracy. We overcome this issue by proposing TSCC; leveraging a Monte Carlo Tree Search methodology to enhance chain inference via an efficient balance between the exploration of label space and the exploration of promising label-set predictions. Results are promising both in terms of predictive and computational performance.
items.title_ko: 분류자 체인을 위한 몬테카를로 트리 탐색
items.summary_ko: 멀티레이블 분류 문제에서 레이블 수가 많거나 훈련 세트에 노이즈가 있거나 누락된 경우의 과제를 다룹니다. 특히 정확한 멀티레이블 평가(predicted set of labels should match the true set exactly)를 최적화하기 위해 '분류자 체인(Classifier Chains)'을 위한 몬테카를로 트리 탐색(Monte Carlo Tree Search, MCTS) 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 멀티레이블 분류 문제의 정확도를 높이는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시하며, 특히 의료 진단과 같이 정확한 레이블 세트 예측이 중요한 분야에서 AI 모델의 성능을 향상시킬 수 있습니다.

items.title: An Automated Framework Integrating Deep Learning and Anatomical Reasoning for Cardiac Phenotyping From CCTA
items.body: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) depicts coronary anatomy and cardiac fat, but segmentation alone does not ensure anatomically consistent measurements. We propose an automated framework that combines deep learning with anatomical reasoning for quantitative cardiac phenotyping. Its anatomical measurement module uses graph geometry, branch identity, and surrounding structures to define vessel-specific pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) sampling and a surrogate epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) compartment. The latter also generates training targets without requiring expert pericardium contours. A companion module quantifies coronary calcium on non-contrast CT. Component-wise benchmarking was conducted on five public datasets: ImageCAS, ImageCAS-X, COCA, Visual Lab, and MultiD4CAD. On ImageCAS-X Test-160, lumen segmentation with validation-selected post-processing achieved a Dice score of 0.9133 and a clDice score of 0.940, exceeding the corresponding published CAS-Net point estimates. In the four-split ImageCAS evaluation, the four-member ensemble outperformed the single ResEnc-L model. Analysis of 800 paired scans showed that PCAT attenuation measurements differed between whole-vessel and lumen references. External EAT evaluation showed strong volume correlation and good spatial overlap. Explicit anatomical rules make the resulting measurements interpretable and inspectable. In practice, the framework provides a standardized pipeline for processing cardiac CT cohorts and quantifying coronary calcium, PCAT, and EAT for population-level analysis and comparison across studies. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/HarryTRAN207/CardiacCT-Research
items.title_ko: CCTA 기반 심장 표현형 분석을 위한 딥러닝 및 해부학적 추론 통합 자동화 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 관상동맥 컴퓨터 단층 혈관 조영술(CCTA) 데이터를 사용하여 심장 해부학 및 심장 지방을 분석할 때, 분할(segmentation)만으로는 해부학적 일관성이 보장되지 않는 문제를 해결합니다. 딥러닝과 해부학적 추론을 결합한 자동화 프레임워크를 제안하여 정량적 심장 표현형 분석을 수행합니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 영상 분석 AI의 정확성과 임상적 유용성을 높이는 데 기여하며, AI 모델이 단순한 패턴 인식을 넘어 의료 전문 지식과 결합하여 복잡한 진단을 수행하는 방법을 제시합니다.

items.title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
items.body: Adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar enables privacy-preserving, all-weather physical scene understanding across darkness, smoke, and walls. However, standard instruction tuning treats continuous radar streams as static text-like tokens, causing near-random global radar-to-text retrieval and severe physical drift under sensor blackouts. Conversely, coupling pairwise contrastive losses (e.g., SigLIP) directly into the shared backbone improves retrieval but injects $O(B^2)$ repulsive gradients that fracture continuous coordinate manifolds ($R^2 < 0$). We present PhysRF-WorldJEPA, a manifold-decoupled Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) that separates continuous electromagnetic state prediction from cross-modal language alignment. An unattenuated 1.0x clock anchor and parallel dual-scale RF encoder feed a lean ~3% LoRA LLM trained with two-step state-space EMA-JEPA (Denoise -> Rollout) and sample-axis Batch-VICReg to predict +3.0 s physical states; a stop-gradient alignment head then maps frozen prompt states onto the text hypersphere with false-negative masking. On a 4,541-window tri-domain suite (77/60.25/60 GHz) against 10 baselines, freezing the physical backbone and training only the decoupled head lifts R->T R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% and improves MedRank from 107.0 to 60.0 while preserving identical physical readout: 3.37 deg ($R^2=+0.961$) blackout +3.0 s torso tilt, 1.89 m ($R^2=+0.679$; 1.19 m/+0.863 at the RF front-end) cluttered UAV altitude, 2.04 m ($R^2=+0.461$) behind-wall NLOS range, 0.9976 virtual-RIS invariance, and 100% fall recall. Across five 0.5B-1.8B LLM families (15 zero-overhead models), World-JEPA improves retrieval and 75%-drop completion in 10/10 runs and blackout tilt in 4/5 (Span-Euc), 2/5 (Scatter), and 5/5 (per-family best) over SFT.
items.title_ko: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: 이질적인 LLM을 매니폴드 분리 밀리미터파 레이더 월드 모델로 변환
items.summary_ko: LLM을 밀리미터파(mmWave) 레이더에 적용하여 프라이버시를 보호하면서 악천후에서도 물리적 장면을 이해하는 문제를 다룹니다. 기존 방법의 한계를 지적하고, 이질적인 LLM을 '매니폴드 분리 밀리미터파 레이더 월드 모델'로 변환하는 PhysRF-WorldJEPA를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 자율 주행 및 로봇 공학에서 프라이버시 보호 및 견고한 환경 인식을 위한 혁신적인 접근 방식을 제시합니다. AI가 열악한 시각 조건에서도 정확한 판단을 내리도록 돕는 중요한 기술입니다.

items.title: Duo: Towards Spatiotemporal Action Coordination in Bimanual Policies
items.body: Bimanual manipulation requires each arm to perform distinct motions while coordinating with the other. Common flow-based robotic policies combine both arms' actions into one token per future timestep, giving attention distinct positions across time but not across arms. We introduce Duo, a simple but effective design that models spatial and temporal dependencies within one shared action head. Specifically, Duo separates both arms into two action tokens per timestep, allowing each arm's motion to interact via cross-arm attention during flow matching. On RoboTwin 2.0, Duo improves the overall success of all four base policies, from 0.45B to 3.62B parameters, with gains of 12.55 and 9.02 percentage points for FLOWER (0.89B) and $π_{0.5}$ (3.62B), respectively. Despite its compact size, FLOWER-Duo achieves the best randomized-generalization, precision, and memory scores on RoboDojo. In real-world tasks, it outperforms $π_{0.5}$ in both success rate and execution speed, while scaling effectively with increasing training data. To provide deeper insight into the design of Duo, we conduct systematic ablations on inter-arm coordination, action grouping, and token granularity, confirming that cross-arm attention drives the improvement while arm-wise interaction offers the best accuracy-compute trade-off.
items.title_ko: Duo: 양손 정책에서 시공간 행동 조정을 위한 모델
items.summary_ko: 양손 조작(bimanual manipulation)에서 각 팔의 개별적인 움직임과 협업이 필요한 문제를 해결하기 위해, 공유된 하나의 행동 헤드 내에서 시공간 의존성을 모델링하는 간단하면서도 효과적인 설계인 Duo를 소개합니다. 각 팔의 움직임을 시간 단계별로 두 개의 행동 토큰으로 분리합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇 공학 분야에서 양손 로봇의 미세 조작 및 협업 능력을 향상시키는 중요한 기술입니다. 복잡한 조작 작업을 수행하는 로봇 시스템 개발자에게 실용적인 설계 가이드를 제공합니다.

items.title: EEGJev: A System One Decision Model and Benchmark for Multi-Task EEG Question Answering
items.body: A single electroencephalographic (EEG) recording can support multiple decoding tasks. Fixed-label tests cannot show how EEG foundation models handle changing questions or options. We introduce EEGJev, a fast decision model that scores candidate answers in one pass. Our benchmark, EEGJev-Bench, covers six question types across 19 public EEG sources. We held the recording and options fixed while switching between questions about attributes paired during training, such as facial expression and the hand participants were asked to use. Across 13 test sources, EEGJev selected a label for the requested attribute with 99.70% accuracy (49.20% under uniform choice). Balanced accuracy for the specific answer was 62.04%. Its 95th-percentile response time was shorter than NeuroLM's on matched validation questions answered individually. EEGJev lets users switch decoding targets by changing the question. With EEGJev-Bench, researchers can test whether new decoders follow the question more reliably, identify the correct answer more often, or both.
items.title_ko: EEGJev: 멀티태스크 EEG 질의응답을 위한 시스템 원 결정 모델 및 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: 단일 뇌전도(EEG) 기록이 여러 디코딩 작업을 지원할 수 있음을 보여주기 위해, 후보 답변을 한 번에 점수화하는 빠른 결정 모델 EEGJev와 6가지 질문 유형을 포함하는 19개 공공 EEG 소스 기반의 벤치마크 EEGJev-Bench를 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: 뇌-컴퓨터 인터페이스(BCI) 및 신경과학 분야에서 AI 기반 EEG 분석의 효율성과 유연성을 높이는 데 기여합니다. 뇌 신호 기반 AI 애플리케이션 개발자에게 중요한 도구와 평가 기준을 제공합니다.

items.title: PreferenceScene: Personalized Indoor Scene Synthesis from Feedback
items.body: Text-to-scene methods turn a short instruction into a furnished 3D room, but the room that a particular person wants rarely comes across fully in words: many preferences surface only when the person sees a concrete room and can point to what they like and dislike in it. We therefore study personalized indoor scene synthesis under hidden user preferences: over several turns, a system shows a 3D scene, and the user, who sees only rendered images of the scene, replies with brief free-form feedback and a satisfaction score. The system must therefore bring the whole room toward the user's preferences from feedback that comments on only part of it at a time. It must also be able to change every part of the room, because a preference concerns not only single objects but the look and atmosphere that surfaces, lighting, textiles, furniture and their arrangement create together. We present PreferenceScene, in which a large language model keeps an explicit estimate of the user's preferences for every design attribute of the room and, after each turn, infers the taste behind the feedback and revises the whole estimate, including the parts that the feedback does not mention. A scene instantiation module builds every estimated value as its own part of the room, so that each of these parts can follow the user's preferences. We evaluate on the test set of a benchmark with 320 instances in ten room types, with a simulated user and a render-based evaluator. PreferenceScene matches the hidden preferences better than five published text-to-scene baselines adapted to the same interaction, and its match rises with every turn. It even surpasses them when they are given the preferences directly, and a vision-language model rates its scenes as the most realistic and functional.
items.title_ko: 사용자 피드백으로 맞춤형 실내 3D 장면 합성하는 PreferenceScene
items.summary_ko: PreferenceScene은 텍스트 명령만으로는 표현하기 어려운 사용자의 숨겨진 선호를 반영하여 개인화된 실내 3D 장면을 합성하는 시스템입니다. 시스템이 제시한 3D 장면에 대한 사용자의 자유로운 피드백을 여러 차례 주고받으며 원하는 방을 만들어냅니다. 이를 통해 실제 사용자가 선호하는 구체적인 디자인을 생성할 수 있습니다.
items.why_ko: 텍스트 기반 생성의 한계를 넘어 사용자 경험을 기반으로 한 3D 콘텐츠 생성의 새로운 가능성을 제시합니다.

items.title: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
items.body: Spatial reasoning in hospitals requires tracking look-alike equipment, interpreting patient-relative directions, and judging passage widths, yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of these abilities. We introduce Clinical3D-Bench, a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions of eight types on egocentric walkthroughs of 373 hospital-room layouts. Layouts follow hospital design guidelines, answers are computed from the 3D scenes, and paired scene states test whether models change their answers when relevant evidence changes. Videos are photorealistic, and ten physicians screened the layouts. Among 35 multimodal large language models (MLLMs), the best open and proprietary models reach 45.7% and 53.6% macro accuracy, against 40.8% for an answer prior and 79.0% for physicians on a subset, and 27 of 32 open models score below 40% on two-way patient-relative directions. Fine-tuning on Clinical3D-45K, our 44,750-question training set, lifts two MLLMs 16-20 points above the best proprietary model. 3D maps given to the fine-tuned MLLM as input go largely unused: replacing them with another video's, even when they are ground truth, barely changes its accuracy. The proposed GeoJeV instead lets the MLLM compute with 3D: it reconstructs a scene memory from each video, selects 3D operations and their arguments from the MLLM's question state, and adds their evidence to its option scores. It achieves the highest accuracy of all evaluated models, narrowing the gap to physicians.
items.title_ko: 병원 환경 멀티모달 LLM의 공간 지능 평가 및 개선 벤치마크, Clinical3D-Bench
items.summary_ko: Clinical3D-Bench는 병원 환경에서 멀티모달 LLM의 공간 추론 능력을 평가하고 개선하기 위한 시뮬레이션 벤치마크입니다. 병원 설계 가이드라인을 따르는 373개의 병실 레이아웃에서 8가지 유형의 3,368개 질문을 통해 장비 추적, 환자 상대적 방향 해석, 통로 폭 판단 등의 능력을 측정합니다. 기존 벤치마크의 한계를 넘어 실제 병원 환경의 복잡한 공간 추론 능력을 다룹니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 분야에서 AI의 실질적인 공간 이해 능력을 향상시키는 데 기여하며, 이는 로봇 지원 수술이나 병원 내 물류 등 다양한 응용 분야에 중요합니다.

items.title: MARGIN: A Risk-Aware Agent for Robot Program Refinement
items.body: Robot-programming agents improve executable control policies through repeated testing and repair, yet binary success saturates while execution risk persists across unseen scenes. We introduce MARGIN, a risk-aware agent that converts successful robot rollouts into actionable evidence for program refinement. Its near-miss margin measures the fraction of the execution budget remaining in the slowest successful development rollout. The agent uses this signal to prioritize fragile programs, guide targeted repairs, and select revisions that preserve development success while increasing execution headroom. An exact safe-racing rule accelerates success-based candidate evaluation. We evaluate MARGIN across LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-90, and Robosuite. In our 80-task LIBERO-Pro reproduction, 78 programs attain perfect development success while accounting for substantial failures on unseen seeds. The near-miss margin predicts held-out failures with an AUC of 0.774, and low-margin programs exhibit 2.97 times higher failure risk. Across two independent evaluation rounds spanning 37 unique LIBERO-Pro tasks, MARGIN reduces executed control steps by 10.7% and 15.0%, with reductions of 18.0-20.0% on LIBERO-90 and Robosuite. Safe racing reduces fixed-sequence candidate-evaluation episodes by 53.5% while retaining identical selections, and paired execution probes improve acceptance decisions by identifying hidden regressions. Together, these results establish near-miss evidence as an effective basis for risk-aware, budget-efficient robot program refinement.
items.title_ko: 로봇 프로그램 개선을 위한 위험 인식 에이전트, MARGIN
items.summary_ko: MARGIN은 반복적인 테스트와 수정을 통해 실행 가능한 로봇 제어 정책을 개선하는 위험 인식 에이전트입니다. 성공적인 로봇 실행을 프로그램 개선을 위한 실행 가능한 증거로 전환하며, 실패 위험이 높은 프로그램을 우선적으로 수정합니다. 이를 통해 unseen 환경에서의 실행 위험을 줄이고 로봇 프로그램의 견고성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇의 자율성과 신뢰성을 높여 실제 환경에서 더 안전하고 효율적으로 작동하도록 돕는 중요한 연구입니다.

items.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
items.body: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used to maximize expensive black-box functions when direct evaluation is costly. In many real-world applications, the high-fidelity objective can be approximated by a series of lower-fidelity models that provide partial but informative signals at substantially reduced cost. Multi-fidelity BO (MFBO) algorithms aim to strategically combine these information sources to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and evaluation cost. However, existing MFBO methods often oversimplify the complex dependencies between fidelity levels or rely on heuristic acquisition functions that lack theoretical performance guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce a new formulation of the MFBO problem as a fused Gaussian Process bandit and develop a corresponding Fused Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (FGP-UCB) algorithm. Our approach accurately predicts the high-fidelity function by fusing multi-fidelity observations through an autoregressive Gaussian Process model and explicitly quantifies the uncertainty arising from parameter estimation across fidelity levels. The proposed method also provides theoretical simple-regret guarantees, overcoming a key limitation of existing MFBO algorithms that lack provable performance bounds. Effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated via both theoretical analysis and empirical studies.
items.title_ko: 다중 충실도 베이지안 최적화를 위한 융합 가우시안 프로세스 밴딧 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 고비용의 블랙박스 함수를 최적화하기 위한 다중 충실도 베이지안 최적화(MFBO)에 새로운 융합 가우시안 프로세스 밴딧 프레임워크를 제안합니다. 저충실도 모델의 부분적이지만 유익한 신호를 전략적으로 결합하여 정확도와 평가 비용 사이의 최적의 균형을 달성하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 기존 MFBO 방법론의 한계를 극복하며 효율적인 최적화를 가능하게 합니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡하고 비용이 많이 드는 시스템 설계, 하이퍼파라미터 튜닝 등 다양한 실세계 문제에서 최적화 효율성을 크게 향상시킬 수 있습니다.

items.title: From Memory Access to Evidence Sufficiency: Diagnosing and Addressing Demand--Evidence Misalignment
items.body: Long-term memory retrieval often returns query-relevant records, but relevance does not guarantee sufficient evidence: answering requires a set of records that jointly satisfies a question's factual, relational, temporal, and state constraints. We study this demand--evidence misalignment through MemPath, an interventional framework that diagnoses failures in memory access, demand coverage, and evidence utilization. Guided by this diagnosis, we propose BiDE-Mem, which represents questions as typed demands and uses them to guide retrieval and evidence organization. We formalize demand--evidence support; in the evaluated compact path, it is conveyed through provenance-aware evidence organization and Reader guidance rather than a separate generative four-state verification step. On LoCoMo, BiDE-Mem improves accuracy by 6.23 percentage points over Mnemis; on LongMemEval, it achieves 91.80%, with strong multi-hop and temporal performance. Supplementary Qwen-Reader evaluations place it first among seven systems on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S under two judging protocols. Ablations and evidence-level analyses show that demand representation, retrieval, and evidence presentation each contribute to answer quality.

items.title: ExpGuard: Guarding Long-Horizon LLM Agents against Corrupted Experience
items.body: Long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents distill past trajectories into reusable experiences. Misleading or adversarial guidance in source trajectories can corrupt these experiences, allowing harmful instructions to persist across tasks and influence future agent actions. Assessing the risks of potentially corrupted experiences poses three challenges: (1) modeling provenance and execution dependencies before experience reuse, (2) learning task-conditioned risk from trajectory outcomes, and (3) repairing risky experiences at online inference. To address these challenges, we present ExpGuard, a framework for retrieval-triggered experience risk assessment and online repair. Specifically, to tackle challenge (1), ExpGuard integrates experience semantics with provenance and execution dependencies in a task-conditioned heterogeneous graph to predict attack and task-failure risks before experience reuse. To enable task-conditioned risk supervision and tackle challenge (2), we conduct matched counterfactual replays of each original experience and its minimally neutralized counterpart from the same task and environment checkpoint, deriving separate risk labels from differences in attack success and legitimate task completion. To tackle challenge (3) at inference time, ExpGuard repairs candidate experiences flagged as high-risk by the graph-based predictor at retrieval and re-predicts their risks before they enter the agent's active experience context. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of ExpGuard in identifying risky experiences and defending agents against experience corruption.
items.body_ko: 장기적인(Long-horizon) 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) 에이전트는 과거 궤적(trajectory)을 재사용 가능한 경험으로 정제합니다. 소스 궤적의 오해의 소지가 있거나 적대적인(adversarial) 지침은 이러한 경험을 손상시켜 유해한 지침이 작업 전반에 걸쳐 지속되고 미래 에이전트 행동에 영향을 미치게 할 수 있습니다. 잠재적으로 손상된 경험의 위험을 평가하는 것은 세 가지 과제를 제시합니다. (1) 경험 재사용 전 출처 및 실행 의존성 모델링, (2) 궤적 결과로부터 작업 조건부 위험 학습, (3) 온라인 추론 시 위험한 경험 복구. 이러한 과제를 해결하기 위해 우리는 검색 트리거 경험 위험 평가 및 온라인 복구를 위한 프레임워크인 ExpGuard를 제시합니다. 구체적으로, 과제 (1)을 해결하기 위해 ExpGuard는 경험 재사용 전에 공격 및 작업 실패 위험을 예측하기 위해 경험 의미론을 출처 및 실행 의존성과 함께 작업 조건부 이질적 그래프(heterogeneous graph)에 통합합니다. 작업 조건부 위험 감독을 가능하게 하고 과제 (2)를 해결하기 위해, 우리는 각 원본 경험과 동일한 작업 및 환경 체크포인트에서 최소한으로 중화된(neutralized) 경험에 대한 일치하는 반사실적(counterfactual) 리플레이를 수행하여 공격 성공 및 합법적인 작업 완료의 차이에서 별도의 위험 레이블을 도출합니다. 추론 시 과제 (3)을 해결하기 위해 ExpGuard는 그래프 기반 예측자에 의해 검색 시 고위험으로 표시된 후보 경험을 복구하고, 에이전트의 활성 경험 컨텍스트에 들어가기 전에 위험을 다시 예측합니다. 광범위한 실험은 ExpGuard가 위험한 경험을 식별하고 경험 손상으로부터 에이전트를 방어하는 데 효과적임을 입증합니다.
items.title_ko: 오염된 경험으로부터 장기 LLM 에이전트 보호하는 ExpGuard
items.summary_ko: ExpGuard는 장기 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) 에이전트가 과거 경험으로부터 유해하거나 오도하는 지침을 학습하는 것을 방지하는 시스템입니다. 경험 재사용 전 출처 및 실행 종속성을 모델링하고, 궤적 결과로부터 작업 조건부 위험을 학습하여 잠재적으로 오염된 경험의 위험을 평가합니다. 이를 통해 에이전트가 유해한 지침을 지속적으로 사용하지 않도록 방지합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 에이전트의 안전성과 신뢰성을 높여 장기적인 자율 에이전트 개발에 필수적인 과제를 해결하며, 잠재적인 오용 위험을 줄이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: The algorithmic behavioral sink: Modeling the transition to irreversible demographic collapse
items.body: In 2025, the vast majority of major global economies reported a Total Fertility Rate below the replacement level of 2.1. This synchronized collapse has persisted despite extensive pro-natalist financial interventions, revealing a structural limitation in conventional linear demographic models. This paper proposes that the ubiquity of mobile internet and Artificial Intelligence acts as a synthetic mating disruptor, precipitating a non-linear phase transition in human pair-bonding dynamics. Treating the marriage market as a complex system governed by thermodynamic constraints, we present a Fermi-Dirac selection model, using national income distributions as the input spectrum and fitted with Japanese longitudinal data to illustrate how digital hyper-reality generates an increasingly prohibitive Marriage Energy Barrier. Our model quantifies a Tech Factor that decouples female mating expectations from local economic realities during initial courtship, a distortion we predict will be severely exacerbated as AI evolves into an emotional substitute. Projections indicate that this substitution effect is accelerating; without intervention, the world post 2040 risks entering an irreversible demographic contraction, as the sudden surge in TFR required for recovery is biologically impossible. Ultimately, this framework explains why traditional financial subsidies fail to reverse falling birth rates and suggests that digital convenience may represent a behavioral Great Filter that erodes the imperative for species persistence.
items.title_ko: 알고리즘적 행동 싱크: 인구 감소의 비가역적 전환 모델링
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 모바일 인터넷과 인공지능이 인간의 짝짓기 역학에 비선형적 위상 전환을 촉진하여 비가역적인 인구 감소로 이어지는 '알고리즘적 행동 싱크' 현상을 제안합니다. 기존의 선형 인구 모델의 한계를 지적하며, AI가 사회 행동에 미치는 광범위한 영향을 분석합니다. 2025년 기준 대부분의 주요 경제국에서 출산율이 대체 수준 이하로 떨어진 현상을 설명하고자 합니다.
items.why_ko: AI가 인간 사회와 행동 양식에 미치는 심층적인 영향을 분석하며, 단순히 기술 발전을 넘어 사회 구조적 변화를 이해하는 데 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: KKT Atlas: Learning Low-Dimensional Local Scenario Models for Contextual Stochastic Optimization
items.body: In contextual stochastic optimization, integrated learning trains conditional models on operational loss, but repeatedly solving stochastic programs with many scenarios is costly. We propose KKT Atlas, which partitions contexts into local charts and identifies a low-dimensional subspace per chart from decision gradients of the scenario cost. It generates shared scenarios by jointly fitting subspace coordinates and context-dependent probabilities. We show that one more scenario than the subspace dimension suffices to approximate the conditional Karush-Kuhn-Tucker optimality condition under regularity conditions, yielding decision and risk bounds under local strong convexity, with generalization error scaling with the compact parameter dimension. On three synthetic problems, Atlas uses 4-18 scenarios per decision versus 500 for direct-solve full-support integrated learning. It attains comparable or lower risk with about $4$-$23\times$ construction and $13$-$61\times$ batch deployment speedups. Atlas also achieves lower risk than clustering-based reduction at matched support budgets. In real-world European grid reserve commitment, Atlas compresses 728 scenarios to 8-9, cutting construction and deployment times by factors of about 4 and 3 relative to full-support integrated learning. Its loss is lowest over 11 quarters and, over 17 later quarters with fixed settings, slightly higher than with full-support integrated learning and significantly lower than with the remaining benchmarks.
items.title_ko: KKT Atlas: 문맥적 확률론적 최적화를 위한 저차원 지역 시나리오 모델 학습
items.summary_ko: KKT Atlas는 문맥적 확률론적 최적화에서 비용 효율적인 솔루션을 제공하기 위해 컨텍스트를 지역 차트로 분할하고, 각 차트에서 의사결정 경사도를 통해 저차원 부분 공간을 식별하는 방법입니다. 부분 공간 좌표와 컨텍스트 의존적 확률을 공동으로 피팅하여 공유 시나리오를 생성합니다. 이는 많은 시나리오를 반복적으로 풀어야 하는 확률론적 프로그램의 높은 비용 문제를 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 의사결정 문제에서 AI 기반 최적화의 효율성과 확장성을 높여 다양한 산업 응용 분야에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Fix How It Acts, Not How It Thinks: Surgical Fine-Tuning of Frontier LLMs
items.body: Open-weight LLMs are competent software engineers, but they sometimes fail at tasks they are otherwise able to do. Often it is not a failure of reasoning. It is a few small missteps over a long trajectory (repeating a step that has already failed, or declaring the task done while a requirement is still unmet) that make the difference. Correcting this calls for a surgical weight update that steers the model toward the right actions without interfering with its reasoning. Such updates, typically learned with LoRA adapters, are often too small to survive merging into a released checkpoint. In our BF16 release, the median weight change is only 1.5% of a single rounding step, and merging loses roughly two thirds of the update's norm. When the same adapter is merged into the mixed FP8/NVFP4 release of the same model, 93% of the update disappears. Instead of increasing the size of the update, we directly train on the surviving part. We introduce merge-aware fine-tuning. Standard LoRA rounds the merged weights to the storage format only at export, so the loss never sees the rounded weights. We instead round the sum of base weights and adapter update to the release format at every training step, keeping the vendor's quantization scales, and compute the loss on these weights. The forward pass matches the serving engine numerics, and the gradient passes straight through the rounding, so the model we train is the model we ship. The loss optimizes only the model's actions and keeps its reasoning close to the base model. Applied to Nemotron-3.5, the recipe improves agentic coding in both the BF16 and the NVFP4 release, by up to 8.4 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and we publicly release both models.
items.body_ko: 오픈 웨이트 LLM은 유능한 소프트웨어 엔지니어이지만, 때때로 수행할 수 있는 작업에서도 실패합니다. 종종 이는 추론의 실패가 아닙니다. 이는 긴 궤적(trajectory)을 따라 몇 가지 작은 실수가(이미 실패한 단계를 반복하거나, 요구 사항이 충족되지 않은 상태에서 작업을 완료했다고 선언하는 등) 차이를 만듭니다. 이를 수정하려면 모델의 추론을 방해하지 않고 올바른 행동으로 유도하는 외과적인 가중치 업데이트가 필요합니다. 일반적으로 LoRA 어댑터로 학습되는 이러한 업데이트는 출시된 체크포인트에 병합될 만큼 너무 작아서는 안 됩니다. 우리의 BF16 릴리스에서 중간 가중치 변화는 단일 반올림 단계의 1.5%에 불과하며, 병합 시 업데이트 노름(norm)의 약 3분의 2가 손실됩니다. 동일한 어댑터가 동일한 모델의 혼합 FP8/NVFP4 릴리스에 병합될 때, 업데이트의 93%가 사라집니다. 우리는 업데이트의 크기를 늘리는 대신, 살아남은 부분에 직접 훈련합니다. 우리는 병합 인식 미세 조정(merge-aware fine-tuning)을 소개합니다. 표준 LoRA는 병합된 가중치를 저장 형식으로 내보낼 때만 반올림하므로, 손실은 반올림된 가중치를 전혀 보지 못합니다. 대신 우리는 모든 훈련 단계에서 기본 가중치와 어댑터 업데이트의 합계를 릴리스 형식으로 반올림하고, 공급업체의 양자화 스케일을 유지하며, 이러한 가중치에 대한 손실을 계산합니다. 순방향 패스는 서빙 엔진 수치와 일치하고, 기울기는 반올림을 직접 통과하므로, 우리가 훈련하는 모델은 우리가 출시하는 모델입니다. 손실은 모델의 행동만을 최적화하고 추론을 기본 모델에 가깝게 유지합니다. Nemotron-3.5에 적용된 이 방식은 BF16 및 NVFP4 릴리스 모두에서 에이전트 코딩을 개선하며, Terminal-Bench 2.1에서 최대 8.4포인트 향상되었고, 우리는 두 모델을 모두 공개적으로 출시합니다.
items.title_ko: 프론티어 LLM의 '행동' 교정을 위한 정밀 미세 조정 기법
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 프론티어 LLM이 추론 능력은 있지만 긴 작업 과정에서 작은 실수로 실패할 때, 그 '행동'을 수정하기 위한 정밀 미세 조정 기법을 제안합니다. 추론 과정은 건드리지 않고, 모델이 올바른 행동을 하도록 유도하는 외과적(surgical) 가중치 업데이트에 초점을 맞춥니다. 이는 모델이 이미 실패한 단계를 반복하거나 요구 사항을 충족하지 못한 채 작업을 완료하는 등의 문제를 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM을 실제 소프트웨어 엔지니어링 작업에 적용할 때 발생하는 한계를 극복하고, 모델의 안정성과 신뢰성을 높이는 실용적인 접근법을 제시하여 개발자에게 유용합니다.

items.title: Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration
items.body: Linear attention replaces softmax attention with a linear formulation, enabling linear-time computation with a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing key-value cache. These computational and memory advantages have attracted growing interest in linear attention for long-context language modeling. However, compressing past information into a fixed-size state causes memory collisions that hinder long-context understanding. Although DeltaNet mitigates memory collisions through delta-rule updates and Gated DeltaNet extends this approach with gating, these mechanisms may also discard information relevant to future predictions. To address this limitation, we introduce Integral DeltaNet, which maintains two complementary recurrent states: a fast-updating delta state that captures current key-value associations and an integral state that preserves a weighted history of the delta state. At readout, the model adaptively combines these states to access information across different timescales. We further derive a chunkwise parallel formulation that enables hardware-efficient training. We evaluate Integral DeltaNet using 340M and 1.3B parameter models trained from scratch on 15B and 100B FineWeb-Edu tokens, respectively. Comparisons with strong recurrent baselines show improved overall performance in language modeling, commonsense reasoning, real-world and synthetic retrieval, long-context understanding, and length extrapolation. We also compare training throughput and activation memory, as well as decoding latency and memory.
items.title_ko: Integral DeltaNet: 적응형 메모리 통합으로 개선된 선형 어텐션
items.summary_ko: Integral DeltaNet은 선형 어텐션의 고질적인 문제인 메모리 충돌을 완화하여 긴 컨텍스트 이해 능력을 향상시키는 새로운 아키텍처입니다. 기존 DeltaNet의 델타 규칙 업데이트 방식에 적응형 메모리 통합 메커니즘을 추가하여 과거 정보를 고정된 크기의 상태로 압축할 때 발생하는 정보 손실을 줄입니다. 이를 통해 긴 컨텍스트 언어 모델링에서 계산 및 메모리 효율성을 유지하면서 성능을 개선합니다.
items.why_ko: 긴 컨텍스트를 처리하는 LLM의 효율성과 성능을 동시에 개선하여 모델의 활용 범위를 넓히는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: More Powerful, Less Verifiable? Mitigating Hard-to-Verify Hallucinations in MLLM's Reinforcement Learning
items.body: Reinforcement learning (RL) strengthens model capabilities through feedback from humans and environments. However, emerging evidence suggests that reward optimization can produce outputs whose errors are harder for humans to detect. To address this issue, we construct ITHV (the Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset), comprising 2,728 visually grounded instances that distinguish between obvious hallucinations, which humans readily detect, and elusive hallucinations, which humans struggle to identify. We then propose DAPO-V, an extension of DAPO that maximizes correctness subject to a budget on verifiability-aware risk. Specifically, DAPO-V combines a verifiability-aware reward with adaptive dual control, where larger penalties are assigned to incorrect responses on questions with lower human verification accuracy. An adaptive multiplier further adjusts the penalty strength according to risk-budget violations. Across three MLLM base models, DAPO-V improves overall accuracy while substantially improving accuracy on elusive hallucination questions by 5.78--9.72 percentage points over accuracy-only DAPO. We further test DAPO-V with a blinded human study, which shows that hallucinations are more readily detected in DAPO-V than those of the base model.
items.body_ko: 강화 학습(RL)은 인간과 환경으로부터의 피드백을 통해 모델 기능을 강화합니다. 그러나 최근 증거에 따르면 보상 최적화는 인간이 오류를 감지하기 더 어려운 결과물을 생성할 수 있습니다. 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 우리는 ITHV(Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset)를 구축했습니다. 이 데이터셋은 시각적으로 기반을 둔 2,728개의 인스턴스로 구성되어 있으며, 인간이 쉽게 감지하는 명백한 환각과 인간이 식별하기 어려운 모호한 환각을 구분합니다. 그런 다음 우리는 검증 가능성 인식 위험 예산에 따라 정확성을 최대화하는 DAPO의 확장 버전인 DAPO-V를 제안합니다. 구체적으로, DAPO-V는 검증 가능성 인식 보상과 적응형 이중 제어를 결합합니다. 여기서 인간 검증 정확도가 낮은 질문에 대한 잘못된 답변에는 더 큰 페널티가 부여됩니다. 적응형 승수(multiplier)는 위험 예산 위반에 따라 페널티 강도를 추가로 조정합니다. 세 가지 MLLM 기본 모델에 걸쳐 DAPO-V는 전반적인 정확도를 향상시키는 동시에, 정확도만을 고려한 DAPO에 비해 모호한 환각 질문에 대한 정확도를 5.78~9.72% 포인트 크게 향상시킵니다. 우리는 또한 블라인드 인간 연구를 통해 DAPO-V를 테스트했으며, 이 연구는 DAPO-V에서 발생하는 환각이 기본 모델의 환각보다 더 쉽게 감지됨을 보여줍니다.
items.title_ko: MLLM 강화 학습에서 검증 어려운 환각 완화 연구: ITHV 데이터셋 제안
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 멀티모달 LLM(MLLM)의 강화 학습(RL) 과정에서 발생하는 '검증하기 어려운 환각' 문제를 다루고, 이를 완화하기 위한 ITHV(Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset)를 구축했습니다. ITHV는 인간이 쉽게 감지하는 명백한 환각과 인간이 감지하기 어려운 모호한 환각을 구분하는 2,728개의 시각적 기반 인스턴스로 구성됩니다. RL 과정이 모델 능력을 향상시키지만, 오류를 감지하기 어렵게 만들 수 있다는 새로운 증거를 제시하며 이에 대한 해결책을 모색합니다.
items.why_ko: MLLM의 신뢰성과 안전성을 높이는 데 중요한 기여를 하며, 특히 의료나 법률과 같이 오류가 치명적일 수 있는 분야에서 AI 적용의 안정성을 확보하는 데 필수적입니다.

items.title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
items.body: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies Effect targets. A shared generation expert learns to jointly predict Effect and an executable action chunk through flow matching, and reuses the sampled pair to generate future video on demand. This allows the controller to execute actions without waiting for video synthesis. We train on more than 20,000 hours of heterogeneous embodied data, excluding unused chain-of-thought data, and accommodate dataset-specific joint, end-effector, and hand-pose representations. Our evaluation uses the Small (8B) configuration on all five benchmarks and additionally evaluates the Large (26B) configuration on RoboDojo. Experiments examine closed-loop manipulation across complementary benchmarks, and comparisons across multiple baseline policies show consistent improvements from Action Grounding.
items.title_ko: EffectWAM: 로봇 조작을 위한 행동 기반 효과 학습 모델
items.summary_ko: EffectWAM은 시각 예측과 실행 가능한 로봇 제어를 연결하기 위한 세 가지 상호 보완적인 구성 요소(Effect, CaPE, Action Grounding)를 통해 로봇 조작 능력을 개발합니다. 'Effect'는 미래 관측치와 현재 관측치 앵커 간의 차이로 시각적 변화를 표현하며, CaPE(Camera Positional Encoding)는 카메라 포즈를 조건으로 풀링을 수행합니다. 이 모델은 로봇이 환경 변화의 효과를 이해하고 그에 따라 행동하도록 돕습니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 시각 정보를 바탕으로 복잡한 조작 작업을 수행하는 능력을 향상시켜, 실제 환경에서 로봇의 자율성과 유연성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Do Clinician-Scored Examples Help LLMs Code ADOS-2 from Hour-Long Transcripts?
items.body: Large language models can apply a written rubric to a transcript, making automated coding of the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS-2) look within reach. A common way to align such a rater with clinicians is to show it expert-scored examples, but whether correct labels improve agreement is rarely tested. We test this for eight speech-based items of hour-long ADOS-2 Module 3 sessions from 48 children, with one local model and a pre-registered, placebo-controlled design. We compare few-shot scoring, an anchored comparison in which the model only judges a child better, similar or worse than scored anchors and a fixed rule gives the score, post-hoc calibration, protocol-based evidence routing and direct scoring of the full transcript. On 40 held-out children, agreement with clinicians was modest, with quadratic weighted kappa between 0.22 and 0.30. Replacing every example's label with a wrong one changed about a third of the few-shot predictions, more often towards the corrupted labels than chance, but did not lower agreement, 0.25 with correct and 0.23 with wrong labels. A larger second model did the same. The anchored comparison did not improve on few-shot scoring, its cross-child judgements were no more accurate than those implied by absolute scores, and routing did not help. Among the registered, uncalibrated arms, direct scoring of the full transcript agreed best at 0.30. Exploratory follow-up analyses found that the model's graded judgements ranked children better than its final scores, that existing batch calibration raised agreement to 0.46 on the same children, and that in controlled synthetic sessions scoring episodes separately did not beat calibrated whole-transcript scoring. Expert-scored examples do not by themselves calibrate model-based clinical raters, and claims of calibration or added pipeline complexity need corrupted-label controls and strong baselines.
items.title_ko: 임상가 평가 예시가 ADOS-2 채점에 LLM을 돕는가?
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 임상가가 채점한 예시가 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)이 ADOS-2(자폐증 진단 관찰 스케줄)를 채점하는 데 도움이 되는지 여부를 평가합니다. 48명의 어린이로부터 얻은 1시간 분량의 ADOS-2 모듈 3 세션 전사본에 대해 8가지 언어 기반 항목을 테스트하며, 전문가 채점 예시를 보여주는 퓨샷 학습이 LLM의 채점 일치도를 개선하는지 검증합니다. 결과는 LLM이 서면 채점 기준을 전사본에 적용할 수 있음을 보여주지만, 예시의 영향은 더 깊이 분석해야 할 부분입니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 분야에서 LLM의 진단 보조 도구로서의 가능성과 한계를 탐구하며, 실제 임상 적용을 위한 AI 모델 훈련의 중요한 고려사항을 제시합니다.

items.title: From Rule-based to Agentic: LLM Agent based Real-time Control of Urban Drainage Systems for Flooding and Sewer Overflow Mitigation
items.body: Real-time control (RTC) for urban drainage systems (UDS) remains hampered by sparse in-network sensing. While heterogeneous multi-modal meteorological early warnings often contain decision-critical information for UDS RTC, none of the existing approaches can exploit such externally-sourced information within the control workflow. Here we introduce AgenticAI-Control, an agentic artificial intelligence framework able to assimilate multi-source meteorological early warnings in RTC. Two coupled large language model agents are integrated to generate control strategies by retrieving meteorological early-warnings and fusing them with domain engineering expertise. Validated via simulation studies of a combined sewer catchment in eastern China across 10 real-world rainfall events, the AgenticAI-Control achieved 69.1-90.6% reduction in aggregated flood and overflow volumes compared to the rule-based baseline control. Rigorously standardized prompt engineering and modular workflow constraints substantially compress performance disparities among four distinct LLMs. Our work establishes AgenticAI as a viable tool to unify multi-source meteorological monitoring and practitioner domain knowledge, surmounting longstanding monitoring limitations of UDS RTC and delivering cost-efficient, robust intelligent control solutions for sensor-sparse sewer infrastructures.
items.title_ko: LLM 에이전트 기반 도시 배수 시스템 실시간 제어: 홍수 및 하수 범람 완화
items.summary_ko: AgenticAI-Control은 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) 에이전트를 기반으로 도시 배수 시스템(UDS)의 실시간 제어(RTC)를 위한 프레임워크입니다. 이 시스템은 이기종 다중 모달 기상 조기 경보를 제어 워크플로우 내에서 통합하여 홍수 및 하수 범람을 완화합니다. 희소한 네트워크 내 센싱의 한계를 극복하고 외부 소스 정보를 활용하여 UDS RTC의 효율성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 복잡한 인프라 시스템을 실시간으로 제어하여 기후 변화로 인한 재난을 예방하고 도시의 회복력을 높이는 데 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Spec-CoFrGeNet: Reparametrizing Continued Fraction Networks for Stable and Accurate Training
items.body: Continued fractions have been shown to be a function class capable of constructing expressive yet parameter-efficient neural networks. These neural networks are not only effective for supervised learning, but also for training LLMs. However, the rational form of this function class introduces poles when the denominator approaches zero, which prior work has avoided by enforcing a small positive (non-smooth) lower bound. We show that performance and training stability can be highly sensitive to the choice of this lower bound. In this work, we introduce a novel transformation of the partial denominators, inspired by its connection to the Green's function in physics, that mitigates the above issue elegantly by constraining the spectra of the constructed tridiagonal Hamiltonian. Our approach further eliminates the need for incremental training used by previous works for stability, thus avoiding involved modifications to standard pre-training procedures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our reparameterization by replacing FFNs with a previously proposed continued fraction architecture for both language and image generative modeling. Across diverse models, such as GPT-2 XL, (nano) Llama-MoE, and Granite, we show that our proposed method achieves performance comparable to the original (FFN-based) architectures while maintaining ~30%-50% parameter savings as before, and in most cases even outperforms the more complicated incremental training baseline. We further demonstrate, for the first time for continued fraction networks, that their effectiveness also carries over to image generative modeling, that utilize diffusion objectives. On a state-of-the-art Diffusion Transformer, we show that our approach again achieves performance comparable to the original FFN-based models with ~30% parameter savings and significantly outperforms the previous incremental training approach.
items.title_ko: Spec-CoFrGeNet: 안정적이고 정확한 학습을 위한 연분수 네트워크 재매개변수화
items.summary_ko: Spec-CoFrGeNet은 연분수(Continued Fraction) 네트워크의 불안정한 학습 문제를 해결하기 위해 재매개변수화 기법을 제안합니다. 연분수 네트워크는 표현력이 뛰어나고 파라미터 효율적인 신경망이지만, 분모가 0에 가까워질 때 발생하는 극점(pole)으로 인해 불안정해질 수 있습니다. 이 연구는 성능과 학습 안정성을 높이는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: 연분수 네트워크의 잠재력을 최대한 발휘하여 LLM 훈련을 포함한 다양한 신경망 학습에서 안정성과 정확도를 개선하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: FlashQLA: Efficient Context Parallelism for Gated DeltaNet
items.body: Gated DeltaNet (GDN) achieves linear computational complexity through recurrent state updates, but sequential dependencies between chunks limit parallelism, particularly for long-context workloads with small batch sizes or limited head-level parallelism per GPU. We present FlashQLA, a context-parallel execution framework for GDN that exposes additional sequence-level parallelism while reducing boundary-state preprocessing overhead. FlashQLA reduces boundary-state preprocessing overhead through decay-aware preparation and extends sequence parallelism across GPUs with Dual CP, which shares summary computation across parallelism levels. Workload-adaptive Auto CP and CP-aware kernel co-design further improve execution efficiency. FlashQLA achieves $1.7\times$-$3.1\times$ forward speedup and up to $4.4\times$ backward speedup over Flash Linear Attention (FLA) on a single GPU. On eight GPUs with context lengths up to 1M tokens, Dual CP achieves up to $4.8\times$ forward speedup and $4.4\times$ speedup for combined forward and backward execution over FLA KCP.
items.title_ko: FlashQLA: Gated DeltaNet을 위한 효율적인 컨텍스트 병렬화
items.summary_ko: FlashQLA는 Gated DeltaNet(GDN)의 선형 계산 복잡도를 유지하면서도 긴 컨텍스트 작업 부하에서 병렬 처리의 한계를 극복하기 위한 컨텍스트 병렬 실행 프레임워크입니다. 순차적 종속성으로 인한 병렬화 제한을 완화하고, 경계 상태 사전 처리 오버헤드를 줄여 추가적인 시퀀스 수준 병렬화를 가능하게 합니다. 특히 작은 배치 크기나 제한된 GPU 헤드 수준 병렬화 환경에서 효율성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: 긴 컨텍스트 LLM의 효율적인 추론과 학습을 위한 성능 최적화에 기여하며, 특히 자원 제약이 있는 환경에서 GDN의 활용성을 높입니다.

items.title: Online Environment Repair for Coding Agents
items.body: Programmatic verifiers provide scalable reward signals for training coding agents with reinforcement learning, yet subtle harness defects and incomplete unit tests allow policies to earn full credit without solving the intended task. Existing training-time defenses intervene either by penalizing suspicious outputs or by filtering flagged tasks and rollouts. However, output penalties leave the underlying verifier exploitable, driving policies to disguise shortcuts under reasoning monitors or zeroing out valid solutions under detector false positives, whereas task and rollout filtering discards or mutes the hardest problems where shortcuts emerge earliest. Pre-training verifier hardening repairs the environment directly, but misses vulnerability classes that surface only as the policy improves during reinforcement learning. In this paper, we propose online environment repair, which leaves triggering rollout rewards unchanged to remove hiding incentives and asynchronously patches exploited environments during training. Candidate repairs triggered by execution invariants or differential fuzzing are deployed only after passing three automated validation gates that block the exploit while preserving valid solutions, canceling detector false positives and enabling structural propagation across repositories without scaffold labels or reference solutions. Across 20 controlled GRPO experiments on heterogeneous software-engineering repositories, online environment repair reduces cumulative reward hacking from 36.9% to 0.06% and improves held-out Pass@8 from 21.7% to 46.7%, consistently outperforming reward-penalty, rollout-filtering, and static-hardening baselines while eliminating zero-shot exploitation on unseen loophole classes.
items.body_ko: 프로그램 방식 검증기(Programmatic verifiers)는 강화 학습을 통해 코딩 에이전트를 훈련하기 위한 확장 가능한 보상 신호를 제공하지만, 미묘한 하네스 결함과 불완전한 단위 테스트로 인해 정책이 의도된 작업을 해결하지 않고도 전체 점수를 얻을 수 있습니다. 기존의 훈련 시간 방어는 의심스러운 출력에 페널티를 주거나 플래그가 지정된 작업 및 롤아웃을 필터링하는 방식으로 개입합니다. 그러나 출력 페널티는 기본 검증기를 악용 가능하게 남겨두어 정책이 추론 모니터 아래에서 지름길을 위장하거나 감지기 오탐 아래에서 유효한 솔루션을 제거하게 만들며, 작업 및 롤아웃 필터링은 지름길이 가장 먼저 나타나는 가장 어려운 문제를 버리거나 무시합니다. 사전 훈련 검증기 강화(Pre-training verifier hardening)는 환경을 직접 복구하지만, 강화 학습 중에 정책이 개선될 때만 드러나는 취약성 클래스를 놓칩니다. 이 논문에서는 온라인 환경 복구(online environment repair)를 제안합니다. 이는 숨기기 유인을 제거하기 위해 롤아웃 보상을 트리거하는 것을 변경하지 않고 훈련 중에 악용된 환경을 비동기적으로 패치합니다. 실행 불변량(execution invariants) 또는 차등 퍼징(differential fuzzing)에 의해 트리거된 후보 복구는 악용을 차단하면서 유효한 솔루션을 보존하고, 감지기 오탐을 취소하며, 스캐폴드 레이블이나 참조 솔루션 없이 저장소 전반에 걸쳐 구조적 전파를 가능하게 하는 세 가지 자동화된 유효성 검사 게이트를 통과한 후에만 배포됩니다. 이질적인 소프트웨어 공학 저장소에 대한 20개의 제어된 GRPO 실험에서 온라인 환경 복구는 누적 보상 해킹을 36.9%에서 0.06%로 줄이고, 보유(held-out) Pass@8을 21.7%에서 46.7%로 개선하며, 보상 페널티, 롤아웃 필터링 및 정적 강화 기준선을 일관되게 능가하는 동시에 보이지 않는 허점 클래스에 대한 제로샷 악용을 제거합니다.
items.title_ko: 코딩 에이전트를 위한 온라인 환경 복구: 버그 있는 검증자를 수정하여 속임수 방지
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 코딩 에이전트 훈련에서 프로그램 검증자의 결함이나 불완전한 단위 테스트로 인해 에이전트가 의도된 작업을 해결하지 않고도 만점을 받는 문제를 다룹니다. 기존 방식의 한계를 지적하며, 온라인 환경 복구(Online Environment Repair)를 통해 훈련 중에 검증자를 동적으로 수정하여 이러한 '속임수'를 방지합니다. 이는 에이전트가 올바른 방식으로 문제를 해결하도록 유도합니다.
items.why_ko: 강화 학습 기반 코딩 에이전트의 신뢰성과 견고성을 크게 향상시키며, 실제 소프트웨어 개발 환경에서 더욱 유능한 AI 코딩 도구를 만드는 데 필수적인 실용적 기술입니다.

items.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
items.body:
I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months.

Here's the video of the talk. In this post I'm going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply.

Coding agents in November 2025

Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5. With hindsight, this was a consequential model.

In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said:

Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. They said that tasks that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 just a few weeks ago are now within reach.

This held up.

Claude Code was 9 months old at that point, having been introduced alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet on February 24th, 2025.

Opus 4.5 was the first model I had used with Claude Code where the default result was generally the right thing. I hadn't been using Claude Code as a daily driver because it didn't feel reliable enough - I had to correct it often enough that it didn't feel like a clear accelerant.

The new Opus changed that. For most of the coding problems I faced on a daily basis, Opus would get them right. It was clearly faster than working through the problems myself.

Also in November, OpenAI released GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex, and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. These had a similar effect on their Codex coding agent: it became reliably useful for many of my coding tasks.

The timing was convenient, because the December holidays were upon us. A lot of people, myself included, spent December tinkering with these new tools to see what they could do. By January we were ready to use them for our actual work.

Fable class models in June/July

We got our first hint of Claude Fable in April, when Anthropic announced Claude Mythos and said that it was too dangerous to release, due to its improved cybersecurity capabilities. Mythos was a model that could not just find security vulnerabilities, it could also figure out how to exploit them.

In June we got to see how good that model was for ourselves, with the release of Claude Fable 5 - a defanged Mythos, that would solve most problems but would actively block you from using it for security work.

After three glorious days... the US government took it away from us. Fable 5 was placed under export controls that effectively banned the model. We wouldn't get it back until July 1st.

For me, Fable was an inflection point because it introduced us to what I now think of as Fable class models. My definition of these:

In June I wrote about how Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive, after I asked it to help fix a display glitch in Safari and it spun up its own pyobjc-framework-Quartz screenshot mechanism and a CORS-enabled localhost logging server to help resolve the bug.

A more recent example of the power of Fable class models is my mysterious beep finder from a couple of weeks ago. I gave Opus 5.5 and then Fable 5.2 access to five WebAudio microphones in a room full of boxes and it was able to triangulate the source of an infuriating mysterious beep to within about 40cm.

Give it a goal, give it the right tools, and watch it cook.

I'd currently class Claude Fable 5, 5.1, 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 as Fable class (I think of Opus 5.5 as "cheap Fable"). GPT-6 Astra got there for me too, and I think the new Gemini 4 Neon may count as well.

These now represent the baseline for what I expect from a frontier model.

3D modeling and game development in September/October

Something interesting happened with frontier LLMs over just the past four months: they got really good at 3D modeling. Set them up with Blender or ask them to write Three.js code and they'll produce credible models of almost anything you ask for.

I first noticed this with Claude Fable 5, but it really kicked into gear with Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and most recently the Gemini 4 family. Here's Gemini 4 Neon's attempt at "Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data", for example.

3D spatial awareness is crucial if you want to use vision LLMs for robotics. I don't know if 3D modeling capabilities are a side-effect of the labs focusing on that or vice-versa.

Back in August I experimented with having Fable 5 build me a raccoon heist game. It had 3D graphics, looked like a game, and played really poorly. GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra did a much better job but the game itself was still pretty dull after the first 90 seconds of play.

I was somewhat relieved that designing a game that was fun appeared to remain a uniquely human pursuit. I even used that in a talk in September to reassure people that us humans still had a role to play!

Then, I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 "This game isn't fun enough yet. Make it a LOT more fun." And it worked. My Command & Conquer-style RTS went from boring to deeply entertaining overnight, after Opus spent 12 hours playtesting new features and rebalancing the gameplay.

Opus 5.5 was the first model I'd used that appeared to understand fun. I've since worked on several little game projects where prompts like "Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful" produced results that kept me engaged for significant amounts of time.

Opus 5.5 came out on September 22nd, 2026. I've been to two different conferences since then where people showed me game projects they'd been working on that really did feel like proper, worthwhile games.

The indie games scene has descended into a full-blown culture war over AI-assisted programming. A lot of people are calling GTA VI the last pre-generative AI blockbuster.

It feels like another inflection point to me.

Is Fable 5.2 an inflection point too?

I'm still trying to decide if Fable 5.2 represents a new inflection point, or just another incremental improvement.

I'm getting so much done with that model right now!

It seems to have taste that almost exactly matches my own. I have been burning through all sorts of gnarly problems that I've been thinking about (or procrastinating on) for several years now. The release notes for Datasette 1.0a42, 1.0a43, and 1.0a44 - plus LLM 0.37, 0.37.1, 0.37.2, 0.37.3, and 0.38 - all in the last three weeks, represent a flood of fixes, features and improvements.

If this does represent an inflection point, the key feature seems to be that if you can imagine and then clearly describe a piece of software, Fable can build it. That's a wild thing to say, but it matches my experience over the past few weeks.

Software development has transformed beyond recognition in the last year. I don't think I'll ever go back to typing most of my code by hand.

Tags: game-design, my-talks, ai, generative-ai, llms, annotated-talks, coding-agents, claude-code, codex, claude-mythos-fable
items.body_ko:
